newsitem.title: USA: NCAA BASKETBALL-TIM DUNCAN OF WAKE FOREST NAMED NAISMITH AWARD WINNER.
newsitem.headline: NCAA BASKETBALL-TIM DUNCAN OF WAKE FOREST NAMED NAISMITH AWARD WINNER.

text.p: Wake Forest centre Tim Duncan, who led the nation in rebounding this season, Sunday was named winner of the Naismith Award as the College Basketball Player of the Year.
Duncan, who decided to return for his senior season instead of entering the NBA draft, averaged 20.9 points and a national-best 14.3 rebounds per game this past season for the Demon Deacons.
Duncan was selected for the prestigious honour over a group of men's finalists that included Ron Mercer of Kentucky, Keith Van Horn of Utah and Raef LaFrentz of Kansas.
Roy Williams, who coached top-ranked Kansas to a 34-2 record this season, was named the Naismith Coach of the Year.
Both Duncan and Williams fell short of their Final Four aspirations in the NCAA Tournament.
Wake Forest was upended by Stanford in the second round, while pre-tournament favourite Kansas suffered a bitter 85-82 loss to Arizona Friday in the Southeast Region semifinals.
Williams has a 249-58 record in nine years at Kansas.
The award for the nation's top women's college player went to Stanford guard Kate Starbird, the all-time leading scorer for Stanford who averaged close to 22 points per game this season.
The women's Coach of the Year honours went to Geno Auriemma of Connecticut, whose top-ranked Huskies are the only unbeaten team in women's college basketball at 33-0.
